articleTitle: Towards a Framework to Assess the Impact of Design Patterns on Software Metrics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Multimedia Computing, Networking and Applications (MCNA)
abstract: Design patterns are reusable solutions to common design problems. They speed up the development process and help to document software systems. This paper presents a framework to assess the impact of design patterns on software metrics. Our proposed framework applies refactoring techniques to generate non-pattern version of a subject system. Then, software metrics have been calculated and compared for both versions; the pattern version and non-pattern version. The proposed framework has been applied to two subject systems and one design pattern. The evaluation results show that there is no consistent behavior of the software metrics between the non-pattern version and the pattern version.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Earthquake Prediction Technique Using Seismic Data
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Multimedia Computing, Networking and Applications (MCNA)
abstract: Earthquakes are natural disasters that can cause severe damage to human life and infrastructure. Therefore, accurate earthquake prediction is crucial for disaster prepared-ness and risk reduction. Recently, machine learning techniques have shown promise in earthquake prediction. In this paper, we present a comprehensive study on the application of machine learning techniques for earthquake prediction. We first review the existing literature on earthquake prediction using machine learning techniques, including neural networks. We then propose a machine learning approach for earthquake prediction, based on analyzing seismic data. The proposed approach uses a convolutional neural network to extract relevant features from the seismic data, and a long short-term memory network to predict the probability of an earthquake. We evaluate the performance of the proposed approach on earthquake datasets from different regions and demonstrate its high accuracy in earthquake prediction. Our study provides a new perspective on earthquake prediction using machine learning techniques and highlights the potential of deep learning approaches for improving earthquake prediction. The proposed approach can be used in conjunction with existing earthquake prediction methods to provide more accurate and reliable predictions, which can help mitigate the potential impact of earthquakes on human life and infrastructure.

articleTitle: On the Reliability of Computer Simulations in Evaluating The Structural Performance of Reinforced Concrete Beams Under Dynamic Load
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Multimedia Computing, Networking and Applications (MCNA)
abstract: This work discusses the reliability of computer simulations and analysis in evaluating the structural performance of reinforced concrete beams under dynamic loads through multiple computer models. The computer simulation using Finite Element Modeling allows for predicting the behavior and failure modes of reinforced concrete beams under impact load. It also highlights material models, the most complicated part of finite element modeling, especially when the material is a composite material like concrete. In this research, a comparison between different materials models used in modeling reinforced concrete beams under dynamic impact loading was completed using LS-DYNA software. LS-DYNA offers several material models that can be used to model a wide range of materials. Additionally, the mesh size sensitivity is discussed. This research discusses the material model selection and formulations used for the different materials, such as concrete, steel reinforcement, supports, and load impactors, in the finite element simulations. Results related to deflection, stress-strain models, and crack patterns are all discussed and compared. Results showed the effectiveness and efficiency of computer models and analysis in realistically predicting and evaluating the performance of concrete beams under dynamic loads. Actual structural testing under dynamic load consumes time and resources, making computer simulations and modeling a powerful and effective tool for engineers to save time and resources.

articleTitle: Detection of COVID-19 Cases from X-ray Images Using Capsule-based Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Multimedia Computing, Networking and Applications (MCNA)
abstract: Coronavirus (Covid-19) disease has spread abruptly all over the world since the end of 2019. Computed Tomography (CT) scans and X-ray images are used to detect this disease. Different Deep Neural Network (DNN)-based diagnosis solutions has been developed, mainly based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), to accelerate identification of covid-19 cases. however, CNNs lose important information in intermediate layers and require large datasets. In this paper, capsule network (CAPSNET) is used. Capsule network performs better than CNNs for small datasets. an accuracy of 0.9885, F1-score of 0.9883, precision of 0.9859, recall of 0.9908 and area under the curve (AUC) of 0.9948 are achieved on the capsule-based framework with hyperparameter tuning. Moreover, different dropout rates are investigated to decrease the overfitting. Accordingly, a dropout rate of 0.1 shows best results. finally, we remove one convolution layer and decrease the number of trainable parameters to 146,752, which is a promising result.

articleTitle: Exploiting MIMO and Cognitive Radio for Improved Performance in Indoor Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Multimedia Computing, Networking and Applications (MCNA)
abstract: Cognitive radio (CR) technology is essential in solving the radio spectrum shortage. It enables unlicensed users to opportunistically share wireless channels with licensed users, which can enhance the performance of emerging wireless networks. To further improve wireless network performance, multiple-Input multiple-Output (MIMO) technology has also been utilized. MIMO antennas can transmit data over multiple independent fading paths, resulting in transmission diversity and multiplexing gains. In this paper, we propose a novel MIMO-aware channel assignment protocol for CR networks (CRNs) with the objective of enhancing the achieved network through-put. The proposed channel assignment selects the best idle channel and MIMO antenna mode for each CR transmission. The proposed protocol aims to increase the number of per-user transmitted packets by jointly utilizing the multiplexing and diversity gains. The proposed protocol's performance is compared to reference protocols, including spatial multiplexing mode (SMM) and spatial diversity mode (SDM). The results indicate that the proposed CR-enabled MIMO-aware channel assignment protocol has significantly enhanced the overall network throughput.

articleTitle: Exploring Pre-service Mathematics Teachers' Perceptions of Teaching using Educational Games
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Multimedia Computing, Networking and Applications (MCNA)
abstract: Despite the widespread appeal of games among students, many teachers are reluctant to use them as teaching aids. The purpose of this preliminary investigation is to assess the attitudes of pre-service mathematics teachers towards the use of didactic games in classroom instruction and the extent to which they are considered competent in this regard. For this reason, 45 pre-service mathematics teachers answered a survey specially developed for this research. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, which calculated frequencies and percentages. According to the findings of this study, teachers have good attitudes toward the usage of games in their classrooms as well as their ability to use them. However, a tiny number of teachers had negative attitudes. This research will help establish professional development opportunities that are of higher and better quality by providing a thorough grasp of teachers' views.

articleTitle: Enhanced Neural Speech Recognizer for Quranic Recitations
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Multimedia Computing, Networking and Applications (MCNA)
abstract: In this paper, we build on our recent efforts to build a Neural Speech Recognizer (NSR) for Quranic recitations that can be utilized by individuals regardless of their gender, age, or experience. In our previous papers, we presented the Quran recitations by females and males (QRFAM) dataset, which is a large benchmark dataset of audio recordings made by male and female reciters from different age groups and proficiency levels. Along with this dataset, we created several baseline NSR systems based on Mozilla's DeepSpeech model using different subsets of the QRFAM dataset for training, validation and testing purposes. In this work, we present our efforts to optimize and improve these baseline models. We show how to improve the WER by up to <tex>$27.34{\%}$</tex> compared to prior work.

articleTitle: Medicinal Plants Recognition Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Multimedia Computing, Networking and Applications (MCNA)
abstract: The use of medicinal plants has been a longstanding practice in traditional medicine worldwide. Accurately identifying medicinal plants is crucial for determining their medicinal properties and potential applications. However, it can be a challenging task due to the complexity of their appearance. Variations in growth stage, lighting, and imaging conditions can make classification challenging, which limits the application of traditional methods for plant identification. This paper proposes a deep learning-based approach that uses a convolutional neural network (CNN) based on the VGG-16 model. With a dataset of 25,686 images, the CNN is capable of learning and representing complex features in images, enabling it to recognize and classify medicinal plants with high accuracy. The proposed approach can efficiently classify plants with different growth stages, lighting conditions, and imaging settings, providing a reliable tool for plant identification. We achieved an impressive recognition rate of 98%, demonstrating the feasibility of using deep learning techniques for accurate plant classification. The proposed approach has enormous potential for providing healthcare professionals and herbal medicine researchers with a reliable tool for identifying herbal plants. the study represents an essential advancement in the use of deep learning techniques for medicinal plant recognition, overcoming the challenges posed by their complex appearance. The proposed approach has farreaching implications and can significantly impact the field of herbal medicine research, enabling researchers and healthcare professionals to identify and classify medicinal plants more accurately

articleTitle: The Theory of Planned Behavior Regarding Artificial Intelligence in Recommendations and Selection of YouTube News Content
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Multimedia Computing, Networking and Applications (MCNA)
abstract: Increased accessibility to YouTube-based news content is further accelerated by the incorporation of artificial intelligence (AI). Notably, the AI in the recommendations and selection of YouTube videos contains specific omnipresent algorithms. This study focuses on the increasing popularity of YouTube-based news collection and on AI in further facilitating and making the content appealing to the audience. The study applied an experimental approach and collected data from 280 respondents in Jordan. Mainly supported by the theory of planned behavior, we found that attitudes and subjective norms (p > 0.000) are strongly associated with the selection process of YouTube content. Moreover, AI is a strong mediator of the attitudes, subjective norms, and content selection of users of YouTube-based news (p > 0.000). Thus, we conclude that AI is a potential variable in further strengthening the intention to use YouTube in searching, selecting, and watching news content. Additionally, we have highlighted the limitations of the study.

articleTitle: Compliant multimedia storage and data extraction from the untrusted and privacy-sensitive edge
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Multimedia Computing, Networking and Applications (MCNA)
abstract: Remote surveillance has been presented by gov-erning bodies as a means to control sustainable harvesting of natural resources. Traditional CCTV-based surveillance systems mounted on board fishing boats are currently being deployed in larger scale to address concerns about sustainable use of ocean resources. With this solution arises challenges related to securing forensic evidence, preserving privacy, and commu-nicating multimedia data in the face of low bandwidth and fleeting satellite connections. In practice, it is challenging, if not impossible, to use state-of-art surveillance technologies for efficient and accurate monitoring and control of the thousand-fold commercial fishing boats involved in commercial fishery. In this paper, we outline the need for a domain-specific distributed multimedia system that can handle extraction and storage of data in untrusted and privacy-sensitive environments. We outline the various measures that were considered when implementing a system for storage and delivery of edge data in the fishery industry. We present our work towards a middleware system that ensures secure storage and delivery of multimedia data for forensic purposes, while preserving privacy of people captured on video, and adapting to the difficult conditions that may arise. We conjecture that deploying a domain-specific monitoring system on the edge solution is a feasible alternative to privacy-infringing CCTV surveillance, and show that deployment of our system is possible despite the constrained resources in edge environments.

articleTitle: The Role of Self-Determination Theory in Adopting Metaverse for Healthcare and Diagnostics among Healthcare Professionals
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Multimedia Computing, Networking and Applications (MCNA)
abstract: Metaverse technology is not a new phenomenon. Yet, its evolving nature has facilitated many fields, including healthcare and diagnostics. Notably, the relevant technology has widely been adopted among healthcare practitioners due to the attributed benefits and factors that further increase its value for medical purposes. The relevant technology is widely adopted worldwide, and United Arab Emirates is of no exception. This research also focused on the factors under the self-determination theory for the metaverse in healthcare and diagnostics in the United Arab Emirates. The researchers applied the cross-sectional design and obtained data from doctors working in different healthcare organizations in the three cities of the UAE. Employing the Structural Equation Modelling for data analysis revealed that Autonomy and Relatedness are two important factors that affect the Virtual Simulation and Perceived Value regarding metaverse technology for healthcare purposes. Besides, Virtual Simulation and Perceived Value further affect Emirati doctors' intention to adopt metaverse technology for healthcare purposes. Overall, the findings supported the study assumptions, indicating metaverse as an integral part of medical practices and diagnostics, as also affirmed under the self-determination theory. This research concluded that the metaverse had revolutionized the healthcare and diagnostics industry in the United Arab Emirates, leading to more efficient and accurate medical treatments. Further, the study limitations are discussed accordinaly,

articleTitle: A Study of Students' Knowledge, Skills, and Attitudes toward the Use of Infographics as a Teaching Tool
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Multimedia Computing, Networking and Applications (MCNA)
abstract: This research investigates students' knowledge, skills, and attitudes toward using infographics as a teaching tool in education and explores the factors influencing these perspectives. Surveying a sample of 211 teacher students at a university in the United Arab Emirates, the study finds that students have a moderately positive level of knowledge, skills, and attitudes toward using infographics in education. Their attitudes toward using infographics were only moderate, which may be attributed to their limited knowledge and skills. The study also shows that factors such as age, major, employment status, and teaching experience do not significantly impact students' views of infographics, which contrasts with previous studies. These findings emphasize the need for educators to develop knowledge and skills in infographics and train teaching personnel in its application as a teaching tool to improve students' educational experience.

articleTitle: Turning Smartphone Camera into a Fungal Infection Detector for Chickpea Seed Germination
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Multimedia Computing, Networking and Applications (MCNA)
abstract: Efficient seed germination is the first and foremost important step in the life cycle of a plant. Early detection of fungal infection facilitates developing and implementing the appropriate disease management strategy. Therefore, the present study aims to monitor chickpea seed germination for possible fungal infection through image processing by using a smartphone camera. The study gathered images every 24 hours for 3 days at 15 seeds. An expert identified the degree of fungal disease infection. Then, the images are analyzed, and two indexes for detecting fungal infection are proposed and compared. The indexes combine the red and blue bands for index 1 and the green and blue bands for index 2. The data obtained from the indexes are used as input for classification using discriminant analysis. Different classifications were performed according to the chickpea's presence or absence and the percentage of chickpeas infection. Moreover, as the input data, we have compared the results of individual index and the use of combined data. The results indicate that by combining both indexes, average accuracy of 96.66 % and precision of 93.33 % were attained. When individual indexes are used, the performance decreases to 81.90 and 82 % for the average accuracy and 63.26 and 54.54 % for the average precision for indexes 1 and 2, respectively. The proposed method can be implemented as a mobile application to be used in the germination monitoring of chickpeas.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Tools in Media and Journalism: Roles and Concerns
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Multimedia Computing, Networking and Applications (MCNA)
abstract: This paper investigates the utilization of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in media and journalism industry, specifically examining their roles in writing, editing, production, and distribution of diverse media content. The paper addresses concerns raised by media academics and professionals about the increasing adoption of these tools. Employing a descriptive-analytical approach, the paper confirms that media and journalism organizations are actively using a variety of AI tools in their work environment. Additionally, the paper sheds light on various concerns identified by scholars and professionals, which include the creation of deepfake news and information, news bias, job displacement, insufficient transparency, and ethical challenges.

articleTitle: Interaction of motion energy with gesture, extroversion, dominance, and collaboration in dialogue
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Multimedia Computing, Networking and Applications (MCNA)
abstract: This paper studies the relationship between conversational features related to gesture, conversational dominance, collaboration, and personality traits. Specifically, we examine the interaction of motion energy and factors associated with dialogues and participants therein. We observe among semiotic types of gesture in dialogue higher motion energy in Beats, Deictics and Iconics than Symbolics, but lower in Beats than arbitrary hand movements. Dominance and collaboration are correlated with motion energy when contentful semiotic gesture types are excluded. Different collaboration scores present different associations on the level of motion energy. The findings quantify the extent to which the motion energy of participants contributes to judgments of dominance and collaboration in dialogue.

articleTitle: Runs in the Family: Malware Family Variants Identification through API Sequence and Frequency Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Multimedia Computing, Networking and Applications (MCNA)
abstract: Malware may be classified into various families according to several factors, such as the method of delivery to an infected computing system, behaviors performed by the malware on an infected system, or through the presence of key characteristics which can be recognized through malware signatures. Additionally, a given malware family may comprise of many variants which perform similarly on an infected system, yet differ from each other in some discernible way. In this paper, we show that understanding this difference in malware behavior among variants of the same malware family is possible through analysis of Windows API system call sequences and their related frequencies. This allows for the identification of changes in malware variant behavior and illustrates the relationships between malware families.

articleTitle: Multi-Label Classification of Emotions in Arabic Tweets From Different Perspectives
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Multimedia Computing, Networking and Applications (MCNA)
abstract: Sentiment analysis has been studied widely in the literature. Despite these many works, there is a lack of works that concentrates on finding the basic emotions behind these sentiments. This problem becomes more challenging in under-resourced languages, such as Arabic. Furthermore, to our knowl-edge, no works have studied this problem from the reader's versus the writer's perspectives. In this work, we study sentiment analysis and basic emotions extraction from the writer's perspec-tive, which is the person who wrote the text, to complement an earlier work of ours focusing on the reader perceptive. Using a dataset of Arabic tweets, we compare the two perspectives. Since each tweet may contain multiple emotions, we use Multi-Label Classification (MLC) techniques. Three classifiers are compared: Decision Trees (DT), Random Forest (RF), and K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN). Prior results showed that the top performing classifier in the case of the reader dataset was RF. For this work focusing on the writer dataset, RF is not a clear winner for all performance metrics under consideration as DT produces competitive results.

articleTitle: Assessing Mutlimedia Based e-Mental Health Service Provision in Canada
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Multimedia Computing, Networking and Applications (MCNA)
abstract: The study aims to provide an overview of e-Mental Health service (eMH) usage in Canada during the pandemic, patients' satisfaction with the services, and their preferences for different e-Mental visit modalities. The study analyzed data from 1184 out of the 12,052 participants in the Canadian Digital Health Survey and found that the majority of patients were satisfied with the eMH portal and the care they received. Usage rates varied by gender, with female patients reporting higher usage rates than male patients, by age, with older patients reporting higher usage rates, and by citizenship, Canadians by birth used eMH services more than others. There was also a significant difference in perceived satisfaction among different visit modalities (video, phone call, etc.). The study suggests improving e-Mental infrastructure and reducing disparities among age, gender, and citizenship to enhance the adoption of eMH services after COVID-19.

articleTitle: The Reality and Obstacles of Using Computerized Educational Games in Teaching the Students with Intellectual Disability
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Multimedia Computing, Networking and Applications (MCNA)
abstract: The purpose of this study was to determine the reality and obstacles of using computer-based educational games in the classroom of students with intellectual disabilities from the perspective of their teachers. The sample of the study consisted of (66) male and female teachers of students with intellectual disabilities. To achieve the objectives of the study, the researchers used a descriptive approach and collected data using a questionnaire. The results showed that the realism level of using computer-based learning games in teaching mentally retarded students was high from the teachers' point of view, while the obstacles to using computer-based learning games among teachers had a medium level. The results showed that there were statistically significant differences in the mean scores of teachers' responses about the obstacles to the use of computer-based learning games in teaching mentally retarded students in Abu Dhabi city based on the type of school (private, public) in favor of teachers from private schools.

articleTitle: Keynote Speech 3: Exploring the Synergy of 3D Integration and Hardware Security
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Multimedia Computing, Networking and Applications (MCNA)
abstract: As the demand for increased transistor density and performance in integrated circuits (ICs) continues to surge, three-dimensional (3D) integration has emerged as a promising technology. By moving beyond traditional two-dimensional (2D) chips, 3D integration unveils new avenues for computing platforms, including high-performance processors and enhanced computation density. This innovative technology offers advantages such as reduced package size, lower power consumption, improved bandwidth, and enhanced computation density. However, like a double-edged sword, 3D integration also brings unique and unexplored challenges in managing the security of 3D ICs. This keynote address delves into the novel opportunities presented by 3D integration for security mechanisms. It explores how this technology can be leveraged to strengthen hardware security, enabling robust protection against evolving threats. Additionally, it sheds light on the potential security vulnerabilities that may arise in 3D ICs, emphasizing the need for careful consideration and proactive measures to address them.

articleTitle: Keynote Speech 1: Integrating Machine Learning and Multi-Agent Systems for Fully Enabling Device-Edge-Cloud Continuum in Complex IoT Worlds
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Multimedia Computing, Networking and Applications (MCNA)
abstract: Recently the device-edge-cloud paradigm is gaining momentum due to the benefits it could provide for the development of highly effective, efficient, and complex IoT ecosystems of diversified scale. However, there are many issues related to unsupervised control aspects that need to be addressed in order to fully realize the approach and make it fully operative in real complex environments. In order to address such issues, in this talk, we propose an holistic integration of machine learning and multi-agent systems to create a data-driven control architecture capable to autonomically monitor and control the device-edge-cloud continuum. This objective is being developed in the context of the Horizon Europe project named MLSysOps (https://mlsysops.eu/). Some use cases will be proposed to elucidate our current findings.

articleTitle: Keynote Speech 2: Bias and Discrimination in AI Systems: From Single-Identity Dimensions to Multi-Discrimination
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Multimedia Computing, Networking and Applications (MCNA)
abstract: AI-driven decision-making has become pervasive in various aspects of our lives, impacting everyone, everywhere, at any time. However, concerns have arisen regarding the discriminatory effects of AI, as evidenced across diverse domains like content recommendation, healthcare, predictive policing, and autonomous driving. The field of fairness-aware machine learning aims to address bias and discrimination in AI/ML models, but most existing approaches focus on discrimination related to a single protected attribute, such as gender or race. In reality, human identities are multi-dimensional, and discrimination can arise from multiple protected characteristics, for example a combination of gender, race and age. In this talk, I will explore fairness and discrimination in supervised learning for tabular data, progressing from traditional single-attribute discrimination to addressing the complexities of multi-dimensional discrimination

articleTitle: Keynote Speech 4: Digital Transition in Precision Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Multimedia Computing, Networking and Applications (MCNA)
abstract: Digital agriculture is revolutionizing the global agricultural sector, aiming to optimize productivity, enhance competitiveness, and mitigate the negative effects on the environment. Precision agriculture, on one hand, is increasingly being adopted in larger areas, while the process of digital transition involves monitoring crops and incorporating artificial intelligence and other technologies to enable more efficient management practices. Therefore, it is crucial to showcase the manifold benefits of digitalization to farmers, ensuring the development of a sustainable and competitive agricultural sector. Furthermore, obtaining accurate and up-to-date information about farming sites offers significant advantages to researchers, the educational community, and even promotes the emergence of agricultural tourism. This speech aims to explore diverse approaches that facilitate the adoption of digitalization in agriculture. Disruptive technologies such as Low Power Wireless Area Networks (LPWAN) can be combined with other established short-range wireless technologies within a heterogeneous network. Additionally, the integration of multispectral images, 3D point-cloud maps, and AI-powered algorithms capable of processing massive amounts of data (AI and Big Data) can create a comprehensive system that enhances vital aspects such as the sustainability of agricultural activities, reduction in the utilization of natural resources, and increased public awareness of these issues. The exchange of knowledge between farmers and experts will yield valuable recommendations to support their transition to more ecologically sustainable farming practices.
